subject.title: fix(discord): retry reply session init conflicts to prevent silent message loss

question: Should reply-session initialization conflicts use layered short transport retries plus shared persistent self-healing, or should one layer exclusively own recovery?
rationale: Signal and Slack establish transport retry precedent, while https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/101920 proposes a deeper self-heal for persistent wedges; their intended composition affects message timing, duplicate risk, and session lifecycle behavior.

options.title: Layer both recoveries
options.body: Use short abort-aware transport retries for transient races and shared fenced self-healing for persistent conflicts, with composition tests and live proof.

options.title: Use shared recovery only
options.body: Remove the Discord retry if shared self-healing demonstrably covers the linked same-thread race without unacceptable latency.

options.title: Use transport recovery only
options.body: Keep per-channel retries and defer recovery of persistent cross-channel session wedges.

recommendation.title: Layer both recoveries
recommendation.body: Use short abort-aware transport retries for transient races and shared fenced self-healing for persistent conflicts, with composition tests and live proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged history shows the broadest ownership across both the Discord dispatch path and shared reply-session lifecycle.
